page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 6 dedicated physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is generous at 96.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags are present for advanced matrix and vector operations, including Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, supported by a 320 MB L3 CPU cache.

A primary architectural feature of the i7ie.3xlarge is its bundled local storage subsystem, providing 7,500 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The server does not bundle dedicated hardware graphics accelerators, relying strictly on CPU resources for computing tasks.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier single-core instruction processing, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,307.0 points and elevated throughput in text processing and small-model language generation. Single-threaded data compression also achieves strong results, evidenced by 34.64 GB/sec in gzip testing. Multi-core compute performance across stress-ng and Geekbench scales moderately within the middle performance bracket, reflecting its 12-thread capacity rather than massive parallel compute scaling.

By coupling high-density DDR5 memory and 7,500 GB of NVMe SSD capacity to a balanced 12-vCPU configuration, the instance delivers a storage-centric architecture. Tradeoffs include a modest vCPU count relative to the substantial memory and storage volume, making it less suited for compute-bound scaling. The instance is suited for intermediate I/O-intensive database engines, distributed transactional stores, search index nodes, caching clusters, and data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.3xlarge is a storage-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for data-intensive workloads requiring extensive memory and direct NVMe capacity. It features an Intel Xeon 8559C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz with 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, backed by a 320 MB L3 cache and AMX/AVX-512 support. The server includes 96.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU allocation, and integrates 7,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network link. The platform exhibits top-tier single-core compute performance and strong memory throughput in benchmark testing, while multi-threaded tasks remain within median performance brackets. Without bundled GPUs, the hardware profile represents a specialized balance of fast storage capacity and high memory density, making it suitable for distributed databases, caching tiers, log search systems, and real-time data ingestion pipelines.
